name: Quantum Computing
tagline: A textbook binary-bet theme: a tiny pure-play universe, pre-profit names that swing 30%+ on a single milestone, and a flagship fund that's really 'quantum + machine learning'.
key_tensions: Thin universe: really only TWO US-listed pure-play ETFs (QTUM, WQTM). Scarcity itself is the finding.
QTUM's name says 'quantum' but its index is 'Quantum Computing AND Machine Learning' — heavily padded with IBM, NVIDIA, Alphabet, Amazon. Theme purity is diluted by design.
WQTM is purer quantum but tiny (~$26M AUM) and brand new (Oct 2025) — real closure & no-track-record risk.
The underlying pure-plays (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) are extremely volatile and mostly pre-profit — binary single-stock risk flows straight through to the ETF.
Data quality: aggregators reported QTUM top holdings at ~13% each, which contradicts its modified-equal-weight ~2% cap (per SEC NPORT + issuer). Cross-check before trusting.
benchmark_note: SOXX (semiconductors) is included as a yardstick, NOT a quantum fund. Much quantum 'exposure' is really semis/AI; comparing shows how much pure-quantum you actually gain (and what you give up in liquidity).

etfs.name: Defiance Quantum ETF

cost.note: 0.40% — cheapest in the theme and reasonable for a thematic fund.

purity.note: Index is 'Quantum AND Machine Learning'; big-tech (IBM/NVDA/GOOGL/AMZN) dilutes the pure-quantum bet.

concentration.note: Modified equal-weight caps names near 2% across ~84 holdings — well spread.

liquidity.note: ~$5.0B AUM, highly liquid; the established choice.

track_record.note: Live since 2018 — longest record in the theme.

etfs.overall: The liquid, diversified, big-tech-diluted way to play quantum.

memo.thesis: A diversified, liquid basket spanning the quantum + machine-learning supply chain. You get genuine pure-play exposure (IONQ, RGTI, D-Wave) but capped near 2% each, cushioned by mega-cap tech — lower volatility than the names themselves, at the cost of diluted 'purity'.
memo.strategy: Passively tracks the BlueStar Quantum Computing & Machine Learning Index using a MODIFIED EQUAL-WEIGHT method that caps single-name weights near 2% and rebalances semi-annually. No active manager; the index rulebook drives everything. Note the index explicitly includes machine-learning/enabling-tech names, not just quantum.

purity_verdict.text: Holds the real quantum pure-plays but surrounds them with IBM, NVIDIA, Intel, Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft. You're buying 'quantum + AI infrastructure', not pure quantum. Know that going in.

memo.sector_geo: Tech-heavy (semis + software + mega-cap), mostly US with some international. Overlaps heavily with semiconductor and AI ETFs — watch for double-counting if you also hold SOXX/AI funds.
memo.cost_context: 0.40% is the cheapest quantum option and fair for a thematic ETF. You pay less than WQTM (0.45%) for far more liquidity.

⚠️ High beta: diversification within the theme doesn't remove the theme's own volatility.

❓ Overlap: significant semiconductor/AI overlap — may duplicate funds you already own.

decision_log.text: Demonstrates the method. Before acting: verify top-10 vs SEC NPORT (resolve the ~2% vs ~13% conflict), pull drawdown vs SOXX, and decide if you want pure quantum (→ WQTM) or diluted-but-liquid quantum (→ QTUM).

memo.thesis: The closest thing to a PURE quantum-computing ETF in the US: a purpose-built index (built with quantum-software firm Classiq) that weights toward actual quantum hardware/software names with little mega-cap dilution. The price of purity is tiny AUM, no track record, and full exposure to pure-play volatility.
memo.strategy: Passively tracks the WisdomTree Classiq Quantum Computing Index — hardware, software, quantum services, enabling tech (quantum chips, post-quantum cryptography). Launched 2025-10-09. Heavier weighting to genuine quantum names than QTUM's equal-weight + big-tech mix.

purity_verdict.text: Built specifically for quantum, vetted with a quantum-software firm. Top holdings are real pure-plays (RGTI, QBTS, IONQ), not mega-cap ballast. This is the bet 'quantum' implies.

red_flags: 🚩 Tiny AUM (~$26M): material risk the fund is liquidated, forcing a sale + taxable event.
⚠️ Concentrated in the most volatile pre-profit pure-plays — binary single-stock risk flows through.
⚠️ Likely wider bid/ask spreads given low volume — a hidden trading cost.

decision_log.text: The pure bet, but unproven and tiny. Before acting: confirm AUM trend (growing or shrinking?), check average spread, and size any position small given closure risk. Compare directly to holding IONQ/RGTI/QBTS yourself — is the 0.45% fee worth packaging?
